title: Web Foundations
description: Can ship HTML, CSS and browser JavaScript — later TypeScript — that a keyboard user can complete, and can inspect DOM, network and storage in DevTools when the page UI conceals a fault.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can mark up a multi-page site with semantic landmarks and labels, write responsive CSS without a UI framework, and complete core interactions with the keyboard — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can attach DOM event handlers and a fetch to a public or test endpoint, capture what the Network tab shows that the page UI does not, and name the same-origin constraint that applies to the request.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently convert a small JavaScript application to TypeScript with domain types instead of unjustified any, test async error paths, and document the build, type-check and test commands.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a broken request, missing label or keyboard trap where the rendered page would look fine, cite the DevTools panel or accessibility check that proves it, and produce a note another engineer can follow to reproduce the fault without a framework.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's page or TypeScript conversion, name a missing landmark, an unjustified any, or a compile-time type treated as runtime validation, and teach when the type checker is not enough on an unfamiliar front-end.
